author: Akien
prose: ah! so lets review the original trouble ticket intentions. trouble tickets are based on the trouble tickets of the western electric number five crossbar that my dad worked in. the are system alarms, intended to contain all the diagnostic information required to understand and resolve the error without having to duplicate the trouble just to understand it. for the first hour or so they were running, we made one key change, a trouble already reported is not reticketed, the existing ticket has a counter that gets incremented. if a trouble originates in an upstream component (for example the inference proxy), the ticket is created, and it's location is part of what's passed back to the caller so the caller can note additional information if needed (that was added recently). trouble tickets are a system alarm, and the ticket itself is of no use once it's resolved. as such, trouble tickets are logging artifacts, even tho they are handled in a special way. so they live in .cairn/logs/cairn/troubletickets and as part of the logging tree, all elemets over 30 days old are deleted as part of the cairn device sleep cycle. tickets announce themselves to the operator, and because of how you and i work together, for that statement you and i are both operators.
